## Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — 2024-11-26

### Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (AD computer account `desktop-b8tqk49.nemotodes.health`) |
| AD domain | NEMOTODES.HEALTH (DC: NEMOTODES-DC.nemotodes.health, 10.11.26.3) |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString exchanges with the DC at 04:49:55 UTC) |

### Malware
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access client).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** Suricata/ET fired multiple exact-match rules on this traffic:
- `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`
- `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` / `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`
- `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`

This is corroborated behaviorally: the client identifies itself with `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, POSTs to `/fakeurl.htm` (NetSupport's standard C2 URI obfuscation), sends `CMD=ENCD` / `ES=1` / `DATA=<encrypted blob>` beacons (NetSupport's native encrypted protocol), and performs a legitimate NetSupport geolocation lookup against `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` that returned the host's real coordinates.

### Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — plaintext HTTP (not TLS) masquerading on port 443. Repeated `POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` beacons every ~60 seconds from 04:50:45 UTC through the end of the capture (~05:43:29 UTC).

**Malicious/suspicious domains**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` (resolves to 193.42.38.139) — flagged by ET as a known "ZPHP" malicious domain, hit both in DNS lookup and as TLS SNI at 04:50:14–04:50:40 UTC. This is the likely delivery/landing site (piracy/"cracked APK" themed lure).
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231) — NetSupport's own infrastructure, queried by the implant for IP geolocation.
- Supporting redirect-chain domains seen immediately before the infection (04:50:00–04:50:16 UTC): `default.exp-tas.com`, `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5), `confirmsubscription.com` (13.56.30.207 / 52.8.34.0) — consistent with a malvertising/redirect chain from a search result to the malicious download site.

**URLs**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (C2 checkin/beacon URL, repeated ~65+ times)
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` (geolocation callback; response payload decodes to `33.7488,-84.3877`)

**Transferred files / hashes**
None recoverable. The initial payload delivery to/from `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139:443) and `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5:443) occurred entirely over TLS, so the dropped executable's filename and SHA256 are not observable in this capture. All C2 beacon bodies after that point are NetSupport's own encrypted `CMD=ENCD` blobs, not file transfers — no plaintext .exe/.zip/.msi objects were carried over any cleartext HTTP stream in the pcap.

### Timeline (UTC)
- 04:49:38 — host boot/NCSI connectivity check, Kerberos logon for `oboomwald`
- 04:49:57–04:50:16 — Bing search → ad-network redirects (`exp-tas.com`, `classicgrand.com`, `confirmsubscription.com`) → landing on `modandcrackedapk.com`
- 04:50:40 — TLS session (SNI `modandcrackedapk.com`) to 193.42.38.139:443 — likely payload drop, encrypted
- 04:50:45 — NetSupport RAT activates: geolocation lookup, then first C2 POST to 194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm
- 04:50:45–05:43:29 — persistent ~60-second C2 beaconing continues through end of capture

**Note:** unrelated background noise in the alerts (SMBv1/EfsRpcOpenFileRaw/NTLMSSP overflow signatures against the DC at 04:49:55–04:50:10) is standard AD domain-join/logon chatter, not additional attacker activity — no exploitation indicators accompany it.
